The parity plan’s prerequisite is not yet met: the three surfaces have three incompatible UI-document protocols. The highest-leverage next slice is a web-to-shared-contract bridge, not another renderer.

### Dependency-ordered gap map

| Order | Gap | Source evidence | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | **Unify the document contract.** Shared contract v1 has 10 canonical node kinds and durable actions/receipts, but web and TUI define separate protocols. | [shared UI contract](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/packages/learner-contracts/src/ui.ts:47), [web protocol](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/ui-protocol/types.ts:8), [TUI protocol](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/tui/ui/types.ts:1) | I1 cannot pass: documents and action state cannot round-trip without semantic loss. |
| P0 | **Web OpenUI is source-program-only, not shared JSON ingress.** The live chat splits ```openui fences and feeds its program to `@openuidev/react-lang`; it does not validate/render `@keating/learner-contracts` JSON. | [chat path](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx:2359), [program parser](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/segments.ts:139), [renderer](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/renderer.tsx:92) | Fails required dual ingress and prevents web from serving as the canonical reference for the shared fixture. |
| P0 | **Web persistence discards OpenUI semantics.** When recording an action, the event-store document is synthesized as legacy generic `openui` with only lifecycle metadata, then separately emits a free-form action payload. Local component state is separately stored in `localStorage`. | [semantic loss at record](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/integration/ui-actions.ts:15), [non-atomic component state](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/renderer.tsx:51) | Cannot meet atomic mutation-plus-receipt, durable retry, or cross-surface restore requirements. |
| P1 | **The live web registry exceeds the shared contract.** It registers `LearningSurface`, `Explanation`, `Callout`, five-mode `Question`, eight-mode scored `Quiz`, `Flashcards`, nested/dependency-linked `StudyPlan`, `ConceptMap`, image, HTML animation, and notes. | [registry](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/library.tsx:424), [question richness](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/library.tsx:107), [plan richness](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/study-plan.tsx:10) | Shared `question` only carries text/choices, `quiz` only simple questions, `study-plan` is markdown resource, and there are no callout, notes, concept-map, or learning-surface semantics. Direct conversion would lose learner-visible meaning. |
| P1 | **Web Markdown has no single reference implementation.** `MarkdownBlock` supports GFM, KaTeX, spoilers, lazy highlighting, runnable-code recovery, and streaming fences. The live assistant panel instead owns a second ReactMarkdown component map, with no spoiler transform or shared streaming-code path. | [full renderer](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/MarkdownBlock.tsx:1), [live chat renderer](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx:2074), [live chat render call](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx:2409) | “Web-reference Markdown dialect” is presently route-dependent. The parity fixture cannot identify one correct web result. |
| P1 | **Mermaid acceptance is broader and less bounded than its declared fixture.** Web passes arbitrary source to Mermaid with strict security and SVG sanitization, but has no input/work cap and caches using only the first 200 characters. The shared fixture declares only 12 grammar families. | [web renderer](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/MermaidRenderer.tsx:181), [declared grammar list](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/packages/learner-contracts/src/rendering.ts:12) | The pack cannot prove “every grammar/directive the web accepts,” including malformed and oversized inputs. Prefix cache keys can also conflate distinct long diagrams. |
| P1 | **Mobile is the closest consumer, but intentionally a subset.** It has bounded GFM parsing, safe links/images, horizontally scrollable tables/code, and all current shared JSON nodes with durable action dispatch. But browser OpenUI source is explicitly never evaluated; Mermaid is bounded flowchart-only; math is displayed as source text; video/animation become external-resource controls. | [Markdown boundary](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/markdown-document.ts:3), [Mermaid subset](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/mermaid-native.ts:18), [JSON-only ingress](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/ui-document-wire.ts:28), [native node renderer](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/UiDocumentRenderer.tsx:153) | This matches the execution plan’s stated partial status, but does not meet M3’s complete web-reference rendering parity. |
| P1 | **OpenTUI is a text transcript, not the canonical terminal learner surface.** The host renders one `TextRenderable` transcript, has only model/thinking/new/abort/shell controls, and imports no shared learner contract. Its separate adapter turns tool results into static cards. | [host](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/tui/opentui-host.ts:36), [command set](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/tui/view-model.ts:27), [static card adapter](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/tui/ui/adapter.ts:35) | T1/T2 are unimplemented: no durable contract actions, Markdown semantics, Mermaid/media handoff model, terminal modes, or recovery. |
| P2 | **Fixture exists, but is not an executable cross-surface acceptance pack.** It lists web features/components and includes one source program plus one shared JSON document, but the surface implementations do not import/execute it. Web Markdown tests are mostly string checks rather than renderer assertions. | [fixture pack](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/packages/learner-contracts/src/rendering.ts:5), [fixture test](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/packages/learner-contracts/test/rendering-fixtures.test.ts:14), [web Markdown test](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/test/markdown-rendering.test.ts:3) | W1/M3/T2 acceptance cannot be evidenced through real persisted message paths. |

The build plan explicitly requires the web renderer as the reference, common persisted fixture paths, both OpenUI ingress forms, and recovery semantics ([plan](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-build.md:190)). The present architecture contradicts that dependency order.

### Exact registry-to-contract loss points

- `Explanation` maps cleanly to `markdown`.
- `Callout`, `LearningSurface`, and `SharedNotes` have no canonical shared node.
- Web `Question` supports choice, text, blanks, classification, and matching; shared questions only support text/choice.
- Web `Quiz` supports scoring metadata and eight question kinds; shared quizzes have the same reduced question shape.
- Web `StudyPlan` has nesting, dependencies, outcomes, links, progress, and course creation; shared plans are markdown resources.
- `ConceptMap` has no canonical Mermaid node, only an indirect Markdown fence.
- `LearningImage` is mostly representable; `LearningAnimation` carries raw HTML, while shared media only allows a resource reference. It must become an explicit safe handoff or a vetted resource, never portable HTML execution.
- `Flashcards` mostly map to a deck, but web’s live action path still lacks shared durable receipts.

### Recommended next slice: C1/W1 “canonical web document bridge”

Do this before extending Mermaid/mobile/OpenTUI rendering:

1. Extend `@keating/learner-contracts` only where semantics are genuinely missing: surface metadata, callouts, rich question/quiz fields, plan graph, Mermaid, notes, and an explicit animation/handoff model.
2. In web, compile trusted browser OpenUI source with the existing parser into that contract. Separately accept canonical JSON directly. Scope both to session/message before persistence, then remove wire source from prose.
3. Render canonical documents on web through adapters to the existing components. Replace the legacy generic-document action recording with shared `UiAction` plus receipt persistence, so success is shown only after a durable commit.
4. Make registry coverage exhaustive: a test must fail when a component is added to `keatingOpenUILibrary` without a canonical mapping or approved handoff.
5. Have web, mobile, and TUI import one fixture package. First acceptance matrix: Markdown fixture, all registered components, JSON/source ingress, partial/malformed/unknown, retry/restart, and action idempotency.

This slice establishes the data path required for mobile and TUI to consume the same meaning. It also converts the existing mobile work from an isolated implementation into a usable parity foundation.

Evidence status: this was a read-only source audit. I did not run browser, device, PTY, or provider journeys. The execution plan’s own latest mobile claim is source/build evidence only, with no accepted physical-device call/result/retry flow ([execution status](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:665)); terminal acceptance remains an explicit future checklist ([terminal gate](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/plans/cross-platform-parity-execution.md:802)).

content.text:
Closure review: not ready to claim rendering parity. The mobile journal is atomic; the web shared path is not connected to it.

1. **P0 — web shared-document actions are not canonical actions and cannot persist the shared document truthfully.**  
   `SharedUiActionEvent` is an unconstrained string/params event, not `UiAction` ([shared-renderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-renderer.tsx:7)). Questions emit `submit_answer` rather than `submit-answer` ([shared-renderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-renderer.tsx:61)); goal and plan checklists omit the required `nodeId`, and goals also omit `stepId` ([shared-renderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-renderer.tsx:79)). The contract requires those fields and exact action discriminants ([ui.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/packages/learner-contracts/src/ui.ts:129)).  
   The web host forwards that generic event with fence metadata ([renderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/renderer.tsx:148)), then `recordOpenUIAction` converts it into a new *legacy* empty UI document rather than recording the supplied canonical document ([ui-actions.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/integration/ui-actions.ts:15)). A checkbox visibly changes before this noncanonical event is even accepted ([shared-renderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-renderer.tsx:81)). This makes web progress/recovery claims untrustworthy.

2. **P0 — the source-to-shared bridge is not in the live web ingress path.**  
   The production chat still passes source fences as `program` ([AssistantChatPanel.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/components/AssistantChatPanel.tsx:2401)); `KeatingOpenUIRenderer` sends that directly to the old React-Lang renderer ([renderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/renderer.tsx:148)). `compileOpenUISourceToSharedDocument` has no production caller; it is only exercised by its unit test. So the bridge cannot provide claimed cross-surface source parity.

3. **P1 — canonical JSON identity is split between fence metadata and document identity.**  
   The parser retains the JSON document’s own `id` ([segments.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/segments.ts:157)), while actions are attributed to independently parsed fence metadata ([renderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/renderer.tsx:148)). A JSON document whose `id` differs from its header/scope will render one document and record actions against another. This also bypasses message scoping for canonical document IDs.

4. **P1 — matching/classification semantics are lossy and `uniqueMatches` is unenforced.**  
   Both renderers flatten a row answer into display strings such as `"prior: belief-id — reason"` ([web](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-renderer.tsx:54), [mobile](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/UiDocumentRenderer.tsx:212)); the durable adapter joins them again as plain text ([ui-action-mutations.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/ui-action-mutations.ts:51)). Item-to-choice mappings and reasons are therefore unrecoverable.  
   More concretely, `uniqueMatches` is merely type-validated ([ui.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/packages/learner-contracts/src/ui.ts:275)); neither renderer prevents the same option from being selected in multiple matching rows ([web](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-renderer.tsx:67), [mobile](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/UiDocumentRenderer.tsx:243)). Invalid matching answers can be durably accepted.

5. **P1 — shared web rendering ignores document lifecycle and surface capability.**  
   `SharedUiDocumentRenderer` always renders interactive controls ([shared-renderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-renderer.tsx:18)); it neither gates controls on `lifecycle === "ready"` nor handles failed/cancelled documents with the canonical retry action. This differs from mobile’s explicit lifecycle gate and retry UI ([UiDocumentRenderer.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/components/UiDocumentRenderer.tsx:100)). A completed canonical JSON `failed` document can appear actionable on web.

6. **P1 — bridge conversion discards source lifecycle and splits a source Question interaction.**  
   The bridge turns a source `Question` group into independent nodes ([shared-bridge.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-bridge.ts:158)) and unconditionally sets the whole document to `"ready"` ([shared-bridge.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-bridge.ts:194)). Per-component lifecycle/resumability and grouped-submit semantics are not represented. It also generates option IDs while preserving label-based matching answers, creating ambiguous grading identity.

7. **P2 — smoke acceptance is stateful, not an isolated acceptance harness.**  
   The `/rendering-smoke` screen mounts real `UiDocumentRenderer` instances without a session or test repository ([rendering-smoke.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/app/rendering-smoke.tsx:37)). Interacting with it writes fixture progress into the user’s learner store. It is useful for manual inspection, but not safe acceptance evidence.

Acceptance status:

- Good: partial source streaming is withheld until complete statements, and incomplete JSON does not render raw wire text ([segments.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/segments.ts:157)). The source animation is correctly reduced to a non-executing handoff ([shared-bridge.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/keating/openui/shared-bridge.ts:175)). Mobile actions do commit learner mutation plus receipt in one SQLite transaction ([records.ts](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/mobile/src/lib/learner-repository/records.ts:545)).
- Focused tests passed: 15 contract/fixture tests, 15 web segment/bridge tests, and 11 mobile record-store tests. They do not exercise production bridge routing, canonical web action dispatch, identity scoping, lifecycle behavior, or matching uniqueness—so they do not cover the blockers above.
